arroz-chaufa.name: Arroz chaufa
arroz-chaufa.summary: A Peruvian fried rice dish from Chinese Peruvian (chifa) cuisine, brought by Chinese immigrants arriving in Peru in the late 19th century.

lomo-saltado.name: Lomo saltado
lomo-saltado.summary: A traditional Peruvian stir-fry of beef, onions, tomatoes and french fries, created within Peru's Chinese "chifa" culinary tradition.

puelche-people.name: Puelche people
puelche-people.summary: An Indigenous people who lived east of the Andes in Chile and southwestern Argentina, largely wiped out by plagues in the late 18th century, with survivors merging into other groups.

valdivia.name: Valdivia
valdivia.summary: A city in southern Chile founded by Pedro de Valdivia, once one of the southernmost outposts of the Spanish Empire and later settled by German immigrants.

tacu-tacu.name: Tacu-tacu
tacu-tacu.summary: A Peruvian dish of fried rice and beans, often topped with steak or eggs, associated with African slaves who arrived in the 19th century.

plaza-de-toros-de-acho.name: Plaza de toros de Acho
plaza-de-toros-de-acho.summary: The oldest bullring in the Americas, opened in 1766 in Lima and built of adobe and wood, seating 13,700 people.

frederic-edwin-church.name: Frederic Edwin Church
frederic-edwin-church.summary: American landscape painter (1826–1900), a central figure of the Hudson River School known for large, dramatic paintings of mountains and sunsets; one of the most famous US painters of his time.

the-heart-of-the-andes.name: The Heart of the Andes
the-heart-of-the-andes.summary: An 1859 oil painting by Frederic Edwin Church depicting an idealized Andean landscape; its sensational New York exhibition made Church America's leading landscape painter.

the-andes-of-ecuador.name: The Andes of Ecuador
the-andes-of-ecuador.summary: An 1855 oil painting by Frederic Edwin Church, his first major and then-largest work, called an early masterpiece of Luminism.

cementerio-presb-tero-mat-as-maestro.name: Presbyter Matías Maestro Cemetery
cementerio-presb-tero-mat-as-maestro.summary: A cemetery, museum and historical monument in Lima, Peru, opened in 1808 as the city's first burial ground outside its churches and holding the remains of notable Peruvian figures.

chimborazo.name: Chimborazo
chimborazo.summary: A stratovolcano in Ecuador's Andes, reaching 6,263 m; because of Earth's equatorial bulge, its summit is the point on the planet's surface farthest from Earth's center.

cyrus-w-field.name: Cyrus W. Field
cyrus-w-field.summary: American businessman and financier (1819–1892) who helped found the Atlantic Telegraph Company and laid the first transatlantic telegraph cable in 1858.

alexander-von-humboldt.name: Alexander von Humboldt
alexander-von-humboldt.summary: A German polymath, geographer and explorer (1769–1859) who traveled extensively through the Americas from 1799 to 1804 and helped found modern geography.

cosmos-humboldt-book.name: Cosmos
cosmos-humboldt-book.summary: An influential treatise on nature and science by Alexander von Humboldt, published in five volumes from 1845 to 1862, arguing that universal laws unify the apparent chaos of nature.

tungurahua.name: Tungurahua
tungurahua.summary: An active volcano in Ecuador's Andes that gives its name to the surrounding province, with eruptions ongoing since 1999.

cotopaxi.name: Cotopaxi
cotopaxi.summary: An active stratovolcano in Ecuador's Andes, the country's second-highest peak at 5,897 m, ranked among the highest active volcanoes in the world.

chota-ecuador.name: Chota Valley
chota-ecuador.summary: The upper valley of Ecuador's Mira River in the Andes, home to Afro-Ecuadorean villages and reputed to produce many of the country's top soccer players.

harper-s-weekly.name: Harper's Weekly
harper-s-weekly.summary: American political magazine published in New York from 1857 to 1916, known for its Civil War coverage and the political cartoons of Thomas Nast.

william-tilden-blodgett.name: William Tilden Blodgett
william-tilden-blodgett.summary: New York City art collector (1824–1875) instrumental in founding the Metropolitan Museum of Art, serving as its first chairman.

albert-bierstadt.name: Albert Bierstadt
albert-bierstadt.summary: German-American painter (1830–1902) famed for monumental landscapes of the American West, including the Rocky Mountains and Yosemite Valley.

the-rocky-mountains-lander-s-peak.name: The Rocky Mountains, Lander's Peak
the-rocky-mountains-lander-s-peak.summary: 1863 landscape oil painting by Albert Bierstadt showing a Native American encampment before a Wyoming peak, which sold in 1865 for $25,000.

boston-athen-um.name: Boston Athenæum
boston-athen-um.summary: One of the oldest independent membership libraries in the US, founded in 1807 in Boston, holding rare books, art and important historical collections.

henry-david-thoreau.name: Henry David Thoreau
henry-david-thoreau.summary: American naturalist, essayist, and philosopher (1817 to 1862), a leading transcendentalist best known for Walden and the essay "Civil Disobedience."

william-h-osborn.name: William H. Osborn
william-h-osborn.summary: American businessman and philanthropist (1820–1894), a railroad tycoon who led the Illinois Central Railroad and was a noted art collector and patron of painter Frederic Edwin Church.

reynolda-house-museum-of-american-art.name: Reynolda House Museum of American Art
reynolda-house-museum-of-american-art.summary: An art museum in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, built in 1917 by Katharine Smith Reynolds and R. J. Reynolds, opened to the public in 1965 and as an art museum in 1967.
reynolda-house-museum-of-american-art.source_title: Reynolda House Museum of American Art

jos-de-san-mart-n.name: José de San Martín
jos-de-san-mart-n.summary: Argentine general (1778–1850) known as the Liberator of Argentina, Chile and Peru, who led the Army of the Andes across the mountains to defeat royalist forces and free Chile in 1817–18.

hannibal.name: Hannibal
hannibal.summary: A Carthaginian general (247–183/181 BC) who led forces against Rome in the Second Punic War, famously crossing the Alps with war elephants to invade Italy.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.summary: French emperor from 1804 to 1814, and briefly in 1815, who rose to power as a general during the French Revolution and led sweeping military campaigns across Europe and the Middle East.

war-of-the-pacific.name: War of the Pacific
war-of-the-pacific.summary: An 1879–1884 war between Chile and an allied Bolivia and Peru over nitrate-rich Atacama Desert territory, ending in a decisive Chilean victory and major territorial gains.

ava-guarani-people.name: Chiriguanos
ava-guarani-people.summary: Indigenous people, formerly called Chiriguanos, who held their lands in the Andes foothills of southeastern Bolivia from the 16th to 19th centuries, resisting the Inca, Spanish and Bolivian states until 1892.

battle-of-ayacucho.name: Battle of Ayacucho
battle-of-ayacucho.summary: The decisive 9 December 1824 battle of the Peruvian War of Independence, in which forces led by Antonio José de Sucre defeated the Royalist army, securing Peru's independence and ending Spanish rule in South America.

juan-gregorio-de-las-heras.name: Juan Gregorio de las Heras
juan-gregorio-de-las-heras.summary: An Argentine soldier (1780–1866) who fought in the Spanish American wars of independence and later served as governor of Buenos Aires province.

uspallata-pass.name: Uspallata Pass
uspallata-pass.summary: An Andean mountain pass linking the Mendoza wine region of Argentina to Santiago, Chile, used by a division of San Martín's army in 1817.

apiaguaiki-tumpa.name: Apiaguaiki Tumpa
apiaguaiki-tumpa.summary: A messianic Guarani leader (c. 1863–1892) who led a rebellion against the Bolivian government, cattle ranchers and missionaries, and is honored today as a national hero.

bernardo-o-higgins.name: Bernardo O'Higgins
bernardo-o-higgins.summary: Chilean military officer and statesman, a major leader of Chile's struggle for independence from Spain; served as second Supreme Director of Chile from 1817 to 1823, the first to head a fully independent Chilean state.

battle-of-chacabuco.name: Battle of Chacabuco
battle-of-chacabuco.summary: An 1817 battle in the Chilean War of Independence in which José de San Martín's Army of the Andes defeated Spanish royalist forces, a major blow to Spanish rule in Chile.

battle-of-kuruyuki.name: Battle of Kuruyuki
battle-of-kuruyuki.summary: 1892 battle near Cuevo, Bolivia, where government forces overwhelmingly defeated the Chiriguano, ending 400 years of their resistance to outside conquest.

sim-n-bol-var.name: Simón Bolívar
sim-n-bol-var.summary: Venezuelan military officer and statesman (1783–1830), known as El Libertador, who led six South American countries to independence from Spain.

gran-colombia.name: Gran Colombia
gran-colombia.summary: A South American republic from 1819 to 1831 covering much of modern Colombia, Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela, formed after independence from Spain.

callao.name: Callao
callao.summary: Peru's main seaport city, founded by the Spanish in 1537 and a key naval hub of the Viceroyalty of Peru; it gained separate provincial status in 1836.

real-felipe-fortress.name: Real Felipe Fortress
real-felipe-fortress.summary: A fortress in Callao, Peru, built to defend Lima and its port from pirates; site of a two-year siege that ended Spanish rule in South America, now a military museum.

valdiviano.name: Valdiviano
valdiviano.summary: A Chilean soup made from dried meat (charqui) and onions, named after the city of Valdivia.

jerky.name: Charqui
jerky.summary: The Quechua word for dried, salted meat, from which the English word 'jerky' derives; similar dried-meat foods exist worldwide under different local names.

ghost-dance.name: Ghost Dance
ghost-dance.summary: A ceremony begun in 1889 by Northern Paiute leader Wovoka, believed to reunite the living with the dead and bring peace; it spread widely and shaped Lakota resistance.

boxer-rebellion.name: Boxer Rebellion
boxer-rebellion.summary: An anti-foreign, anti-Christian uprising in North China (1899–1901) by the "Boxers," a martial-arts movement, ultimately defeated by an alliance of eight foreign powers.

clorinda-matto-de-turner.name: Clorinda Matto de Turner
clorinda-matto-de-turner.summary: Peruvian writer (1852–1909) whose controversial writings inspired women across Latin America and led to her exile in Argentina.

mercedes-cabello-de-carbonera.name: Mercedes Cabello de Carbonera
mercedes-cabello-de-carbonera.summary: A Peruvian writer (1845-1909) and early feminist who helped pioneer literary realism in Peru, known for novels like Blanca Sol that criticized women's lack of opportunities and Lima's elites.

indigenismo.name: Indigenismo
indigenismo.summary: A Latin American political ideology concerned with the relationship between the state and Indigenous peoples, seeking greater inclusion and recognition of Indigenous rights.

jos-santos-chocano.name: José Santos Chocano
jos-santos-chocano.summary: Peruvian poet, writer and diplomat (1875–1934) known by the pseudonym 'El Cantor de América,' widely praised in Europe and Latin America; he was later stabbed to death on a tram in Santiago.

jos-mar-a-eguren.name: José María Eguren
jos-mar-a-eguren.summary: Peruvian post-modernist writer (1874–1942), mainly a poet but also a journalist, painter, and inventor.

jos-de-la-riva-ag-ero-y-osma.name: José de la Riva-Agüero y Osma
jos-de-la-riva-ag-ero-y-osma.summary: José de la Riva-Agüero y Osma: Peruvian lawyer, historian, writer and politician (1885–1944) who served as Prime Minister of Peru and was a leading figure of the conservative Generation of 900, leaving most of his fortune to Lima's Pontifical Catholic University, which later founded an institute in his name.
jos-de-la-riva-ag-ero-y-osma.source_title: José de la Riva-Agüero y Osma

juana-manuela-gorriti.name: Juana Manuela Gorriti
juana-manuela-gorriti.summary: An Argentine writer with ties to Bolivia and Peru who served as First Lady of Bolivia from 1848 to 1855; her 1851 novel La quena made her Argentina's earliest novelist.

pedro-cieza-de-le-n.name: Pedro Cieza de León
pedro-cieza-de-le-n.summary: Spanish conquistador and chronicler (c. 1518–1554) whose Crónicas del Perú is considered fundamental to understanding Inca history and the empire's structure.

aurora-c-ceres.name: Aurora Cáceres
aurora-c-ceres.summary: Peruvian and Uruguayan writer (1877–1958) associated with the modernismo literary movement, who wrote novels, essays and travel literature.

albert-einstein.name: Albert Einstein
albert-einstein.summary: German-born theoretical physicist (1879–1955) who developed the theory of relativity and won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.

francisco-moreno.name: Francisco Moreno
francisco-moreno.summary: Argentine explorer and academic (1852–1919), known as Perito Moreno, credited as a key figure in Argentina's incorporation and development of Patagonia; the Perito Moreno Glacier is named for him.

perito-moreno-glacier.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
perito-moreno-glacier.summary: A glacier in Argentina's Los Glaciares National Park, fed by the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, and one of Patagonia's most visited natural attractions.

southern-patagonian-ice-field.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
southern-patagonian-ice-field.summary: The world's second-largest contiguous extrapolar ice field, straddling the Andes between Chile and Argentina, a remnant of the last-glacial Patagonian Ice Sheet.

physalis-peruviana.name: Physalis peruviana
physalis-peruviana.summary: A South American nightshade plant, called Cape gooseberry or aguaymanto, whose cultivation traces back to the Inca Empire and which later spread worldwide, sometimes becoming invasive.

ribes.name: Ribes
ribes.summary: A genus of roughly 200 flowering plant species native mainly to the temperate Northern Hemisphere, including redcurrants, blackcurrants, whitecurrants and true gooseberries.

gate-of-the-sun.name: Gate of the Sun
gate-of-the-sun.summary: A monolithic stone gateway at Tiwanaku in Bolivia, carved by the Tiwanaku culture around AD 500–950 and decorated with carvings thought to have astronomical significance.

tiwanaku.name: Tiwanaku
tiwanaku.summary: A major pre-Columbian archaeological site in Bolivia near Lake Titicaca, home to an estimated 10,000 to 20,000 people around 800 CE, with monumental structures and megalithic stonework.

antig-edades-peruanas.name: Antigüedades peruanas
antig-edades-peruanas.summary: An 1851 archaeological study of pre-Columbian Peru by Mariano Eduardo de Rivero y Ustáriz, considered the first scientific work on Peruvian archaeology.

uti-possidetis.name: Uti possidetis
uti-possidetis.summary: A legal principle originating in Roman law, later used in international law to justify territorial claims based on existing possession, including by newly independent states.

aymara-people.name: Aymara people
aymara-people.summary: An Indigenous Andean people of about 2.3 million living mainly in Bolivia, Peru, Chile and Argentina, who came under Inca and then Spanish rule.

litoral-bolivia.name: Litoral
litoral-bolivia.summary: A province in Bolivia's southwestern Oruro Department, with its seat at Huachacalla.

department-of-tarapac-peru.name: Tarapacá
department-of-tarapac-peru.summary: A coastal province, later department, of Peru central to its nitrate industry, occupied by Chile in 1879 and formally ceded after the War of the Pacific in 1883.

ecuadorian-peruvian-war-1857-1860.name: Treaty of Mapasingue
ecuadorian-peruvian-war-1857-1860.summary: The 1860 treaty ending the first Ecuadorian-Peruvian War, in which Ecuadorian General Guillermo Franco agreed to Peru's territorial demands; both governments later disavowed it.

putumayo-department.name: Putumayo
putumayo-department.summary: A department in southern Colombia bordering Ecuador and Peru, with its capital at Mocoa; its name comes from Quechua words meaning 'gushing river'.

julio-c-sar-arana.name: Julio César Arana
julio-c-sar-arana.summary: Peruvian rubber baron and politician, 1864 to 1952, whose company carried out the Putumayo genocide against Indigenous Amazonians before he later served as a senator.

university-of-the-andes-venezuela.name: University of the Andes (Venezuela)
university-of-the-andes-venezuela.summary: The second-oldest university in Venezuela, based in Mérida, and the largest public university in the Venezuelan Andes, with one of the country's biggest student bodies.

federation-of-the-andes.name: Federation of the Andes
federation-of-the-andes.summary: An 1826 proposal by Simón Bolívar to unite Colombia, Peru and Bolivia into one confederation, which never came about due to political disagreements.

arica.name: Arica
arica.summary: Chile's northernmost port city, near the Peruvian border, an important trade outlet for landlocked Bolivia and site of ancient Chinchorro mummy finds.

tarapac.name: Tarapacá
tarapac.summary: A town in the Tarapacá region of Chile, sharing its name with the region.

agust-n-gamarra.name: Agustín Gamarra
agust-n-gamarra.summary: A Peruvian soldier and politician who served twice as President of Peru (1829–1833 and 1838–1841); of mixed Spanish and Quechua descent, he died in battle during a failed invasion of Bolivia.

antonio-jos-de-sucre.name: Antonio José de Sucre
antonio-jos-de-sucre.summary: Venezuelan general (1795–1830) and close associate of Simón Bolívar who led key victories in South America's wars of independence and served as Bolivia's first president, from 1825 to 1828.

peruvian-amazon-company.name: Peruvian Amazon Company
peruvian-amazon-company.summary: A rubber company operating in the Peruvian Amazon in the late 1800s and early 1900s, notorious for enslaving and abusing Indigenous workers, exposed by a 1912 British investigation.

jos-antonio-p-ez.name: José Antonio Páez
jos-antonio-p-ez.summary: Venezuelan military officer and politician (1790–1873) who fought for independence under Simón Bolívar, later led Venezuela's separation from Gran Colombia, and served three times as president.

central-university-of-venezuela.name: Central University of Venezuela
central-university-of-venezuela.summary: The oldest university in Venezuela, founded in 1721 in Caracas, with a main campus that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site designed by architect Carlos Raúl Villanueva.

napo-river.name: Napo River
napo-river.summary: A roughly 1,075-km tributary of the Amazon River that rises in Ecuador on the flanks of Andean volcanoes including Cotopaxi.

mapuche-religion.name: Ngünechen
mapuche-religion.summary: One of the most prominent deities in Mapuche religion, sometimes equated with the Christian God.

mariano-melgar.name: Mariano Melgar
mariano-melgar.summary: Peruvian poet, artist and soldier in the war for independence from Spain, celebrated for romantic love songs called yaravíes; he died in 1815 at age 24.

venezuelan-declaration-of-independence.name: Venezuelan Declaration of Independence
venezuelan-declaration-of-independence.summary: Document adopted by Venezuela on 5 July 1811, declaring separation from Spain and founding the new nation on equality and free expression after three centuries of colonization.

chinese-peruvians.name: Tusán
chinese-peruvians.summary: A term for Peruvians of Chinese descent, from a Chinese word meaning 'local born'; Peru has Latin America's largest population with Chinese ancestry, tracing back to 19th-century laborers.

san-mart-n-de-los-andes.name: San Martín de los Andes
san-mart-n-de-los-andes.summary: City in Argentina's Neuquén province at the foot of the Andes, founded in 1898 as a military outpost and now a major tourism destination.

chapelco.name: Chapelco
chapelco.summary: A mountain and massif in Neuquén Province, south-western Argentina, later developed into a ski resort founded in 1946.

la-oroya.name: La Oroya
la-oroya.summary: A city in central Peru's Andes, known for a smelting operation that made it one of the world's most polluted places, and as the eastern end of the country's Central Highway.

huancayo.name: Huancayo
huancayo.summary: Capital of Peru's Junín Region, founded in 1572 in the Mantaro Valley; historically home to the Huanca people before their incorporation into the Inca Empire.

andes-industrial-science-009: Royal University of San Buenaventura of Mérida de los Caballeros
andes-industrial-philosophy-001: Royal University of San Buenaventura of Mérida
andes-industrial-philosophy-008: Real Universidad de San Buenaventura de Mérida
